Shri Justice Radhakishan Agrawal Judgment on Board 14/12/2023 1.
Heard on I.A. No.1 of 2023.

2. This is an application for condonation of delay of 215 days in filing the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32653 MAC.
3.

For the reasons mentioned in the application, which is duly supported by an affidavit, the same is allowed and delay of 215 days in filing the MAC is condoned.
4. Also heard on admission.
5.

This appeal is by the appellants / claimants against the award dated 22.09.2022 passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fast Track Court, Mahasamund, C.G. in Claim Case No.114/2021, awarding total compensation of Rs.15,69,600/- with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of application till realization, fastening the liability on the Insurance Company.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fast Track Court, Mahasamund, C.G.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties shall hereinafter be referred to as per their description before the Tribunal.

6. As per averments in the claim petition, on 15.03.2021 at about 9:00 pm, deceased Rameshwar Shrivas, aged about 36 years, earning Rs.15,500/- by running a hotel and betel shop, was returning from village Rajim to Fingeshwar by driving Eco Van bearing registration No.CG04-LQ-5614.

However, on the way, when he reached near village Borsi, driver/non-applicant No.1 of the vehicle Metador bearing registration No.CG06-GP-1321 (hereinafter called as 'offending vehicle') by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the vehicle of deceased, as a result of which deceased- Rameshwar Shrivas sustained grievous injuries over his body and died on the spot.
At the time of accident, the offending vehicle was owned by non- applicant No.2 and insured with non-applicant No.3/Insurance Company.

7. On claim petition being filed by the claimants under Section 166 of the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32653 Motor Vehicles Act for compensation to the tune of Rs.38,40,000/-, the Tribunal considering the evidence led by both the parties passed an award as mentioned in para 4 of this judgment.

8. The only ground urged by learned counsel for the appellants/claimants is that the monthly income of the deceased has wrongly been assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.8,450/- per month,
whereas it should be Rs.15,500/- per month looking to the nature of work of the deceased.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 / Insurance Company supported the impugned award while submitting that the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.8,450/- per month as per the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, which needs no interference by this Smt. Sunita Shrivas vs Ashok Kumar Banjare on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53620396/
2 Court.

entities.text: Sunita Shrivas vs Ashok Kumar Banjare
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also submits that the Insurance Company has not filed any appeal against the impugned award.

10. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award.
11.

As regards the income of the deceased, it appears from the record that though the claimants have pleaded in the claim petition that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by running a hotel and betel shop, but no documentary evidence, licence or certificate to run the shop has been adduced by the claimants to substantiate the said fact.

Therefore, in these circumstances, in absence of any cogent and reliable evidence regarding income, the Tribunal, considering the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, C.G. issued by Labour Commissioner-cum-Competent Authority, Chhattisgarh,
Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32653 Raipur, assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.8,450/- per month, which cannot be faulted with.

Further, the Tribunal after granting amounts under the other heads, awarded a total compensation of Rs.15,69,600/- in favour of the claimants with interest @
7% per annum from the date of application till its realization, which, in the considered opinion of this Court, is just and proper.
12. In view of above, I do not find any scope for enhancement in this appeal, warranting no interference by this Court.
13. Resultantly, the appeal being without any substance is liable to be dismissed at the admission stage itself and is, accordingly, dismissed.
